cur:catacombs-praetextatus-good-shepherd.summary: A ceiling decorated with red lines, garlands and small birds centres on a medallion in which the Good Shepherd stands among his sheep, a lamb across his shoulders. A crack runs across the vault, but the gentle, airy decoration still conveys the peace and paradise-garden imagery with which Roman Christians surrounded their dead.
facts: Commons and Wilpert date the painting to the second half of the 3rd century.
Painting reproduced from Joseph Wilpert, Die Malereien der Katakomben Roms (Freiburg, 1903), whose plates were photographed in the catacombs and hand-coloured in front of the originals.
cur:catacombs-praetextatus-good-shepherd.notes: The Good Shepherd in funerary art is a symbolic image whose identification with Christ is an interpretation; in this Christian catacomb it is generally accepted.
